highlights.title: Android can now securely migrate your logins between password managers
highlights.summary: As longer, more complex passwords have become a necessity, remembering all those strings of numbers, letters, and special characters has become nearly impossible. Password managers can solve that problem, but what happens when you want to move to a different login organizer?
body: Google designed the new login transfer process to happen entirely on your phone, so you need the corresponding apps installed with your credentials synced. To start the move, you’ll have to find the import option in the app you want to use. The location of that feature will vary, but in Google Password Manager (built into Android), it’s near the top under the settings tab.

The import option in Google Password Manager will plug in to the new migration system, while export still just creates an unencrypted CSV with your passwords that can be dumped into any app. It will be similar in other apps, so make sure to start the process in the app you want to use. Currently, this works in Google’s app, 1Password, Bitwarden, and Dashlane.

Once you trigger the migration, the Android system will verify your identity and ask you to confirm the move in your new password manager. Android can move both passwords and passkeys without creating any risky text files. Even if you’ve got a lot of passwords, the process should wrap up quickly.

highlights.title: How a researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT to search for new antimicrobial molecules
highlights.summary: César de la Fuente’s lab uses Codex and ChatGPT to search living and extinct genomes for antimicrobial candidates to fight drug-resistant infections.
body: César de la Fuente and his lab probe the genomes of living and extinct organisms for molecules that could help fight drug-resistant infections.

Drug-resistant microbes including bacteria, fungi, parasites, and viruses are a growing global threat. About five million deaths in 2021 were associated ⁠ (opens in a new window) with bacterial antimicrobial resistance—an annual toll projected to roughly double by 2050. It can take years to find molecules with the potential to become antimicrobials. Researchers are using AI to accelerate this early stage of discovery.

“Antimicrobial resistance is one of the greatest existential threats to humanity in my opinion,” said César de la Fuente ⁠ (opens in a new window), a bioengineer whose cross-disciplinary lab searches for antimicrobial candidates. “And yet, we haven’t had a new class of antibiotics for 50 years.”
Much of modern antimicrobial development focuses on modifying existing medicines or searching familiar classes of chemicals. But that approach offers diminishing returns.

body: England piled on 453 runs to establish a commanding first-innings lead of 320 in the third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.
The hosts were firmly in control and on course for a 3-0 series sweep, with Pakistan closing on 52-2, still 268 runs adrift, when rain curtailed play.
"I've liked the tempo of the batting in this series," former England captain Hussain said.
"We talked about it earlier in the Bazball era, England going too hard and not seizing opportunities.

highlights.title: Final Fantasy 7's Future in Fortnite Is Unclear, but There’s Hope
highlights.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi spoke about Square Enix's relationship with Fortnite in a recent interview. Although he didn't directly answer whether Final Fantasy characters would eventually be part of Fortnite 's extensive roster of skins, some hope lingers among fans.
body: Fortnite 's latest season, Chapter 7 Season 4, has two main themes: video games and hacking. Combining the two made it possible for Epic Games to bring an array of new video game IPs to its Battle Royale. This season, players can snag cosmetics inspired by Sonic the Hedgehog, Crash Bandicoot, Mega Man, and Spyro. There are many more to come, with confirmed upcoming appearances from Kingdom Hearts ' Sora and Persona 5 's Joker.

"What I can say right now is that, looking back at the history of Final Fantasy 7, fans might notice this, but we haven’t had a lot of very major collaborations with other IPs. This is mostly because we wanted to be selective to protect the brand of Final Fantasy 7. But what I can say now is that we are, you know, considering a lot of, you know, different collaborations at the moment. So, you know, whether Fortnite is included in the list of potential collaboration partners, that’s something for the fans to look forward to."
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

highlights.title: Meta’s Muse AI works and creeps me out
highlights.summary: Meta has launched its new Muse assistant, marking the company's first real foray into AI-powered productivity tools. The company says its AI agent can "take the busywork off your plate" by helping you with online shopping, emails, trip-planning, and more.
body: One of the first tasks I assigned Muse, which carries out actions using a cloud-based virtual computer, was to sort through my Gmail inbox and delete messages I don’t need. That required me to connect Muse to my Google account and give it permission to access, read, and delete emails. The process didn’t go smoothly on mobile; the Google sign-in screen kept glitching and returning me to the Muse website instead of the app. I eventually got it working on my laptop, where it deleted thousands of promotional emails and updates. I didn’t feel good about permitting Muse to view all of my emails given Meta’s track record on privacy over the years.

highlights.title: Russell: I have an answer to Antonelli's pace
highlights.summary: George Russell insists he does "have an answer" to Kimi Antonelli's pace but admits he will need good fortune to catch his Mercedes team-mate at the top of the Drivers' Championship.
body: ​​​​​​Russell suffered a demoralising blow to his already faint title hopes at last weekend's Italian Grand Prix when he was beaten to victory by Antonelli despite the 20-year-old having started from 19th on the grid after receiving a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance.
The result saw Russell, who had started second in Monza, fall 66 points behind Antonelli with 10 rounds remaining, starting with this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid.
Russell started the season as the clear title favourite but has won just two grands prix compared to Antonelli's seven, with the Italian being consistently quicker, especially in terms of race pace.
Asked about finding himself in situation where he doesn't have an answer to Antonelli's speed, Russell replied: "I do have an answer and I'm working on it, and it's been much improved.

highlights.title: Wardogs Surpasses 1 Million Copies Sold on Day One, Blows Past 300k Peak Concurrent Players on Steam
highlights.summary: Wardogs has already surpassed a million copies sold and is lighting up Steam's concurrent player charts. Earlier today, developer Bulkhead launched its brand new all-out warfare FPS, Wardogs.
body: “To cross a million copies sold as we launch into early access is mental,” said Joe Brammer, CEO at Bulkhead. “We've spent the last few months showing people exactly what Wardogs is, what it isn't, and at one point literally gave everyone ten reasons not to buy it. We didn't want people buying into blind hype. So seeing more than one million people choose to jump in and play the game at early access launch means a huge amount to all of us. But this is still early access. We've got things to fix, things we want to improve and a lot more we want to build. The best thing players can do now is keep playing, keep telling us what they think and keep giving us those ridiculous Wardogs moments.”

Wardogs is currently only available on PC, making its debut sales numbers all the more impressive, but it is coming to consoles. Bulkhead confirmed that Wardogs is targeting a 2028 release for PS5 and Xbox, but didn't offer a concrete release date. The developer has also noted that it expects the hype to die down eventually, as they plan to take their time when it comes to releasing new content and therefore there may be drops in player counts.

highlights.summary: Below you can see the latest top games and companies by downloads and revenue for August 2026, as well as the big stories and trends from the last month. Data is provided by AppMagic. Check out profiles of the world's top publishers in the Top 50 Mobile Game Makers 2025 list.
body: Note that these estimates are based on gross revenue from player spending across the App Store and Google Play only. It does not feature estimates from alternative marketplaces or direct-to-consumer platforms.

Aniplex’s long-running gacha Fate/Grand Order has seen player spending spike to its highest monthly sum of the year. The game made $57.7 million this August with an anniversary celebration in Japan, more than doubling July’s $22.5m.

In fact, this was the anime-style RPG’s best month since last August. The game makes 89% of its earnings from Japan, meaning the month is a major one each year - more than the North American anniversary in early July.

On a daily spending basis, earnings reached their highest in more than five years this August. Fate/Grand Order generated $4.6m on the 15th, surpassing any daily record from the past five anniversaries but not quite matching the game’s lifetime high of $5.6m on January 1st, 2021.

highlights.title: Is ‘Vintage Violence’ the Future of Movies? Inside the Frantic Chase Movie Built for Phone-Addicted Audiences: It’s a ‘New Approach to Viewing’
highlights.summary: Eugene Kotlyarenko’s “Vintage Violence” is a movie that speaks directly to America’s phone-obsessed culture. The kinetic action adventure, which has its world premiere Sept.
body: Kotlyarenko, whose previous film was the similarly internet-minded 2020 thriller “Spree,” says the online style was essential for the story he wanted to tell.
Even though Kotlyarenko’s technique is extremely modern, he is comforted by knowing that some of cinema’s greats are also into pushing visual and tech boundaries.

“One of the great adventures and joys of trying to innovate something is using those cinematic techniques and finding inspiration in other filmmakers,” he says. “There are filmmakers who seem very technologically in tune, like Brian De Palma, or Pedro Almodóvar is always doing something that feels very contemporary technologically. So I’m looking to what’s cool about how the masters think about stuff and then trying to put my own energy and spin on it.”

Another important visual element came from nodding to Japanese film culture, as so much of the movie was shot there with a local crew. Kotlyarenko, along with his DP Sean Price Williams, was able to experiment in the footsteps of Japanese cinema legends.

highlights.title: Panic builds over bankrupt Spirit’s looming data sale to Google
highlights.summary: Doug Kreuzkamp was shocked when news outlets reported that Google won an auction to buy a huge amount of operational data as part of Spirit Airlines’ bankruptcy proceedings.
body: Kreuzkamp founded a startup called Springshot in 2011, which created a widely used proprietary platform that helps humans and AI systems improve airline efficiency and quickly solve logistics problems so flights can stay on time and airlines can operate as smoothly as possible. Hundreds of airports use it globally.

Springshot powered Spirit’s technology stack for the last three years, right up to the “very last flight,” Kreuzkamp told Ars. Yet his company got no notice when Spirit prepared to auction off a massive dataset that he thinks likely improperly includes a substantial amount of data and intellectual property (IP) that Springshot owns—not Spirit.

In a limited objection filed last month, Springshot argued that Spirit’s sale agreement does not make it clear what data is being sold. It only vaguely references categories of data that would possibly rope in Springshot data, including “productivity and collaboration data,” “core business systems and business application data,” and “workflow and process data.”

We’re introducing a new Data agent in ChatGPT Work ⁠ (opens in a new window) to help more people answer those questions themselves. body: Dead or Alive is a fighting game franchise with a fiercely loyal fanbase and a dedicated competitive scene. Despite these factors, it’s also known as the fighting game series with the most fanservice — a label that’s hard to get away from, given the jiggle physics, dating-sim-heavy spinoff games, and sexy outfits that exist in abundance in almost every DoA title.

While Dead or Alive 7 is in active development, DoA 6 Last Round is still getting content, including a new character that was just announced yesterday. Minato’s addition to the roster hasn’t come without controversy; some fans are accusing the schoolgirl of being a copy/paste of Honoka, while others are pointing toward a September 9 Famitsu interview that included some divisive remarks from the game’s development team.

Of these remarks, one is standing out from the rest: Project Manager Tsuyoshi Iuchi confirmed that Koei Tecmo is making the decision to step back from making more sexy outfits for Dead or Alive’s characters. This is a big change for the franchise, and one that’s been met with backlash and confusion from its fanbase.

highlights.title: Physicist does the math on Star Trek’s “Picard maneuver”
highlights.summary: It turns out Jean-Luc Picard was an even better starship helmsman than the writers knew. A physicist has gone through the details of a warp-speed trick from the first season of Star Trek: The Next Generation and found a subtlety the show missed.
body: Níckolas de Aguiar Alves, a physicist at the Federal University of ABC in Brazil, first watched Next Generation as a master’s student. When he got to the episode “The Battle” in the show’s first season, the plot reminded him of his relativity coursework.

In “The Battle,” a Ferengi leader reminds Picard of a battle he fought years ago as captain of a ship called the Stargazer. Under fire from a mysterious attacker, Picard’s ship’s shields were down. He had to get closer without taking a hit, so he made a gamble. Picard ordered the Stargazer to charge the enemy ship at warp speed (meaning faster than light), then stop abruptly and fire. By going faster than light, Picard anticipated that the other ship would see two images of the Stargazer: where it reached warp speed and where it stopped. If they fired on the wrong image, they would miss the Stargazer, and Picard could win the battle.
Later in the episode, Riker mentions that the trick had been immortalized in Starfleet textbooks as the “Picard maneuver.”
points: It turns out Jean-Luc Picard was an even better starship helmsman than the writers knew.

highlights.summary: Another researcher is challenging OpenAI about the data driving its increasingly impressive array of mathematical discoveries. Just days after a bitter row erupted over whether the company's models benefited from unpublished work, a second mathematician has come forward accusing the AI giant of…
body: In a series of posts on Mastodon, mathematician Andreas Thom raised concerns that interactions he and his colleagues had had with the ChatGPT chatbot before OpenAI’s triumphant announcement may have contributed to its success in the field. One of the 10 results OpenAI announced with great fanfare last month involved Thom’s area of expertise, so-called non-sofic groups, and OpenAI acknowledged that their result built heavily on previous work by Thom and fellow mathematician Gábor Kun.

Thom said he began reflecting on his own interactions with OpenAI after Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematics professor at New York University, publicly questioned whether the company’s AI models had benefited from his use of OpenAI’s Codex. After OpenAI announced its non-sofic groups result, it was widely criticized in mathematical circles for failing to acknowledge recent contributions from Thom and Kun and the company quietly amended its writeup. Non-sofic groups are, roughly speaking, infinite mathematical structures that cannot be approximated by finite ones.
points: Another researcher is challenging OpenAI about the data driving its increasingly impressive array of mathematical discoveries.

highlights.title: A scientist said bananas ‘kill’ the benefit of blueberries. Is that true?
highlights.summary: Can blending these popular fruits in a smoothie adversely affect the berries’ nutritional benefits? Experts weigh in. This year was shaping up to be a banner year for bananas: they were lauded as “ 2026’s big viral taste ”, landed pride of place as Prada’s new lip balm flavor, and were even deemed…
body: But this summer, the Mel Robbins Podcast featured Dr Rhonda Patrick, a biomedical scientist, who said that adding banana to a blueberry smoothie could adversely affect the nutritional benefits of the berries.
Could the beloved mashup of blueberries and bananas really be a bad match?

Patrick’s claim involved an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase, which appears in bananas, and polyphenols, an umbrella term for a diverse family of antioxidant compounds found in plants – including blueberries.

“Polyphenol oxidase, it’s essentially an enzyme that’s breaking down the polyphenols. And there have now been studies … showing if you add bananas to blueberries, you’re not getting as many polyphenols. In fact, it’s quite a bit lower. So the banana is killing the benefit,” she said.

highlights.title: Powering AI is an architecture problem
highlights.summary: On July 22, 2026, a transmission line fault in Ashburn, Virginia—the heart of the world’s largest data center cluster—knocked more than 3 gigawatts of load off the grid in seconds. And it wasn’t the first time.
body: The AI power debate is mostly about generation: more turbines, more solar, more transmission. The grid needs more electrons. But the outages in Virginia weren’t supply failures; they were architecture failures. And a giant wave of interconnections is arriving on that same architecture, putting grid reliability at risk. It’s a problem nobody wants to own.

The grid was built around predictable loads: steel mills, refineries, and houses at dinnertime. Different load sizes, same process—drawing power smoothly, misbehaving occasionally, and recovering gracefully.

An AI campus can swing 70% of its load in milliseconds during a training run, then trip offline just as fast at the first sign of trouble upstream to protect billions in compute. Each is rational alone. Together, at gigawatt scale, they’re a problem the grid has never solved—and the next wave of data center campuses is planned at exactly that scale.

The standard data center power stack hasn’t changed in decades. Medium-voltage power arrives, transformers step it down, low-voltage uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units condition it, and it reaches the racks. Push that design to AI scale, and it cracks in three places.

highlights.title: The iPhone Duo Might Be One of the First Foldables That's Good For Gaming
highlights.summary: I've been hooked on foldables for years now, and I carry the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra on me every day. And while that phone is incredible for most of what I need to do on a day-to-day basis, gaming has never felt amazing on it.
body: A big part of that comes down to the aspect ratio of the larger inner screen. While there are a lot of games that will adopt the 4:3 aspect ratio, there are plenty that just don't, leading to either an ugly, stretched picture or giant black bars. In Hearthstone, for example, I have the choice of having a third of the screen blocked off, or have it stretch out to fill the screen, only to cut off a good portion of what's supposed to be displayed.

There have been several times where I've tried to fullscreen that game, only to not be able to read a card on one of the far edges of the battlefield, because the image is cut off. Now, a lot of this does come down to the developers. Certainly, Blizzard has the resources to update Hearthstone to accommodate the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's square display. But, I've been testing these foldables for the last seven years and things haven't improved. If Blizzard hasn't done anything by now, I doubt it's going to any time soon. I'd rather not leave it up to individual developers here.

highlights.title: Clearview AI Is Testing an AI Tool That Would Let Cops Unearth Your Life Online
highlights.summary: InquiryIQ, a previously unreported prototype, tested a model from xAI, maker of Grok, to surface associates, social accounts, and other information about people identified through Clearview.
body: In 2020, face-recognition firm Clearview AI became infamous for scraping more than 3 billion photos from the internet to turn faces into names for police and security professionals. Now the company is experimenting with trawling the web again, this time using AI to potentially help law enforcement fill in the person behind the name—who they are, who they know, where they live, and what they’ve left behind online.

Clearview has quietly built and tested what it describes as an experimental AI “analyst assistant,” WIRED has learned. Called InquiryIQ, the unreleased tool is designed to take details an investigator unearths from a Clearview search and then automatically fan out across the web—opening webpages, analyzing images, and assembling what it finds into a profile containing the possible employers, aliases, associates, and physical characteristics of a person police are investigating.

body: The US will stage the 2031 World Cup and World Rugby is seeking to capitalise commercially despite mounting fears over the parlous state of rugby union in the host country. As a result, the governing body is desperate to raise interest in the sport’s profile by staging high-profile matches Stateside, with Baltimore hosting the fourth Test between South Africa and New Zealand on Saturday.

A failed attempt was made to attract the British & Irish Lions to stop in Las Vegas on the way to Australia in 2025, though England did face the USA in Washington that summer while the All Blacks and Ireland met in Chicago last autumn. The 2030 finals weekend of the Nations Championship has also been slated for the United States.

Taking a Six Nations match to America would be an altogether more significant move given how financially valuable home championship fixtures can be to the competing unions. But World Rugby is willing to help bridge the shortfall and has floated Ireland v Italy as a potential fixture, given the number of expats from each country on the east coast.

highlights.title: Wardogs Has A Massive Start On Steam, But Players Face Brutal Server Queues
highlights.summary: A big new military FPS, Wardogs (not to be confused with the 2016 Jonah Hill/Miles Teller crime-comedy War Dogs) launched today in early access on Steam, and it's off to a hot start.
body: Given the flood of players, developer Bulkhead instituted a server queue system, and this quickly became something of a meme on social media. Players shared screenshots of the queue and their place in it--some people reported having more than 300,000 people in line in front of them. Yeesh.

Bulkhead responded to the brutal queueing situation, saying it was partly due to the developer being "rate limited." The company said it was working with Valve to resolve this limit and get an increase in line with "larger titles."
Things got worse, temporarily albeit, for some, as Bulkhead made the decision to kick everyone from the queue as a fix that, in theory, would help more players get into the game faster.

Bulkhead boss Joe Brammer gave an update on the queuing situation, saying the queue itself is not "specifically broken," but instead he said Wardogs didn't get the kind of treatment that AAA games receive when it comes to rate limits.
